scope: Exact nonsingleton rank-zero anchor-restoration palette split, physical alternate table, shared-secondary two-attack witness ladder, and the 16-vertex equality sharpness control only.

clean_room_control.control_conclusion: The attacked-secondary row has movers 5 and 7 and a legal dominating banned nonretained alternate {1,7,10}; the shared-secondary row has only mover 7 because 1-5 is a graph nonedge. Both rows meet at retained banned state {1,5,10}.

review_findings: The C-149/C-163 synchronous rank-zero semantics are preserved exactly.
Lemma 2.1 correctly proves u in Q(r) and q outside S before arbitrary-state restoration is applied to two literal outside vertices.
Theorem 2.2 exhausts the attacked-anchor versus shared-anchor secondary split and makes no graph-nonedge inference from palette omission.
The physical alternate is r->a, is legal iff ar is an edge, and its endpoint is banned iff q lies in B.
Proposition 3.2 uses two unoccupied attacks with unique one-guard responses and has the claimed externality boundary.
The control is a sharp obstruction to promoting a dominating banned alternate, not a closure of the full-list branch.
nonclaims: The three color traces cannot coexist.
The universal gamma-theta conjecture is resolved.
Literature priority for the equality control is established.
